items.note: Lemon hero band with a 96px centred headline, ringed by five different thick ink-outlined objects. The largest (envelope, pencil, notepad) are about 200–250px and cropped by one side edge or the bottom seam, so the rc.2 sticker-scale gap has mostly closed and the composition weighs like the reference's coin hero. Below it come a white-framed featured card and a vignette card grid. The hero action is still a small single pink button, where the reference has a large black block CTA with a bordered search beside it.

Four stickers of at least about 120px are cropped by the side edges around a big headline and a full-width pink CTA, then a black seam leads into the paper body. This is close to how the reference phone bands keep their large cropped objects rather than shrinking them. The lone CTA is the only weak point against the reference's black CTA and search pair.

Black bar with a white current pill and a pink full-height CTA block, as in the reference dark capture. The lemon hero and its stickers are unchanged, and the featured card is a raised dark panel. The hero band's bottom edge simply meets the black ground with no visible ink seam, where the reference closes every field with a line.
The dark bar, a raised menu button and an unchanged lemon hero with side-cropped stickers carry the reference's dark mode faithfully. Hierarchy (headline, lead, CTA) reads as clearly as in light.

Lemon header band with breadcrumb, bold article title, meta and outline tag pills over a paper body. The prose column and a white 1px-ink 'on this page' box are now aligned to one left edge, which closes the rc.2 alignment gap. Quiet and well spaced, in the manner of the reference's product chrome (set 06).

Band, ink-framed contents box and generous prose follow the reference's phone chrome. In the band, though, the breadcrumb breaks after its link and repeats the full title on a second line right above the large title. The header is tall and says the title twice, where the reference keeps its breadcrumb to one short line.

Unchanged lemon band on black, light prose and a raised contents panel with a hairline, as the dark recipe asks. The band's bottom edge has no ink seam against the black ground, so the band floats rather than being closed off as in the reference.

Dark bar, unchanged lemon band and a raised contents panel. The type scale and spacing match the light version and stay in the reference's language. The repeated-title breadcrumb is the same as in light mode.

Same considered article chrome: band, aligned prose, contents box, a rounded pull-quote and a teal media box with a thick paper-slip vignette. The code sample is still a flat grey box with a grey border, the one surface outside the reference's white or raised, 1px-ink set (this was named in rc.2 and is still open).

Lemon band, white ink contents box and readable prose all match the reference's phone screens. The band again breaks the breadcrumb and repeats the title right above the large title, which makes the header heavier than it needs to be.

Dark article with raised panels and an unchanged band and vignette. The code sample becomes a mid-grey slab rather than a raised panel with a hairline, so it reads as a different material from the rest of the page.
Dark bar, lemon band, raised contents panel and light prose. The reference's dark recipe is applied cleanly, with the same hierarchy as light.

Periwinkle header band with a section-size title, a lead and one thick clipboard sticker cropped by the trailing edge. Below it, a paper body with headings and an author list drawn as one ink-framed group divided by rules, as in the reference's hairline-frame language. The sticker is about 150px, a little under the band size, but it reads as a solid object, not a fragment.
The band keeps its clipboard sticker at about 160px, cropped by the right edge beside the title block, and the reference's phone band character holds. Body type and spacing are generous and calm.
Black bar with a white current pill and a pink CTA block. The periwinkle band and sticker are unchanged, and the author group is a raised panel. This matches the reference dark treatment.
Same faithful dark adaptation: an unchanged band with a side-cropped sticker and light prose on black. Hierarchy is as clear as in light mode.

findings.summary: The front-page hero's only action is a compact pink button about 48px tall, with no bordered field beside it. The reference anchors its hero with a large black block CTA paired with a bordered search field of the same height, a two-part action row that carries real weight under the headline.

Code samples in articles are a flat grey box with a grey border in light mode and a mid-grey slab in dark mode. The reference builds every box as white or the raised tone with a 1px ink hairline. This was named in rc.2 and is still open.

On phones, the article header band's breadcrumb wraps after its link and spells out the full article title on its own line, directly above the large title. The band says the title twice and grows tall. The reference keeps the breadcrumb to one short line, so the title leads.
In dark mode, colour bands end straight on the black ground with no 1px ink seam. The hero and article bands look pasted on rather than closed off. The reference ends each field at a visible seam.
